risk_reasons: The change edits the Release cycle's P4 candidate scan, which the SolicitationReleasePoller runs on the Railway worker every tick
It re-spells an entitlement gate (subscriptionGrantsFullAccess) inside SQL; an over-exclusion starves an account that could still send
It edits an allowlisted platform-wide scan, so scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts gains a table entry and a baseline bump
Its evidence is a live-DB integration suite, not a unit suite
goal: An account the Release cycle refuses at the account level stops occupying candidate slots in selectReleaseCandidates' oldest-first scan, for BOTH account-level refusals — account_cap and subscription — each arm refusing EXACTLY the accounts its per-account gate refuses, while the account_cap and subscription withhold counters keep arriving on a fully excluded tick.
non_goals: Joining auto_approval_policies INTO the candidate scan (amended 2026-09-19 after the owner re-decided: the caps are read in their own statement and resolved in TypeScript, so the scan binds numbers rather than re-deriving the clamp)
Any second SQL spelling of LEAST(configured, 10) — resolveAccountDailySendCap stays the single owner of the enforced number
Any state change to a lapsed account's rows: edge case 4 requires the rendered rows to survive so paying inside the window resumes the drip
Changing the gate order, the ReleaseWithheldReason union, or any per-account gate in runAccountArm
Changing past_due grace behaviour anywhere else in the product
Adding a glossary term (docs/context/solicitation-send-mode-breaker-release-attribution.md is 47 words under its 3,000-word cap)
Touching the three peer sweep scans (P1, P2, P3, P5) or the Veto anchor scan
user_visible_behavior: Operationally: a tick whose candidate window was held by a lapsed account now releases for the other accounts instead of releasing nothing
A Release cycle report on a tick where every candidate account lacks full access carries withheldByReason.subscription = <number of excluded accounts>, where it previously carried an empty map
An account both at its cap and without full access is reported ONCE, under account_cap, matching runAccountArm's gate order
A trialing account is never excluded by the new arm: it has full access
No owner-facing surface changes; no row state changes
invariants: Neither arm over-excludes: the subscription arm binds the array subscriptionGrantsFullAccess is implemented over, and the cap arm binds resolveAccountDailySendCap's OUTPUT, so each refuses exactly what its gate refuses
resolveAccountDailySendCap stays the single owner of the enforced per-account cap: it is called in TypeScript and its numbers are bound into the scan; LEAST(configured, 10) never appears in SQL
ONE policy read per tick feeds both the cap arm and every per-account cap gate, so the two can never disagree about an account's number
Invariant #11: entitlement is gated on subscriptionGrantsFullAccess, never a raw equality against 'active'
Invariant #15: release.ts keeps taking sql as an explicit parameter and imports no db singleton
The candidate predicate is spelled ONCE, in the eligible CTE; the exclusion counts come from the same set via the LEFT JOIN, never from a second statement
Both counters arrive on a tick that returns zero candidate rows
The account_cap counter keeps its current meaning and value: COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) over the capped half of eligible
A lapsed account's outreach rows stay delivery_status = 'rendered'; nothing is terminalized
ci:tenant-scope stays green with an exact-match baseline bump, and ci:static-policy stays green with no new subscription-status literal allowlist entry
edge_cases: Account capped AND lapsed: excluded once, counted under account_cap only, never under both
Account lapsed with status past_due: excluded (the release gate grants no grace; only subscriptionAllowsDashboardRead does)
Account lapsed with status pending_payment or cancelled: excluded
Account with status trialing: NOT excluded, releases normally
Every candidate account lapsed: zero candidate rows, withheldByReason.subscription carries the account count, releasePhaseStoppedBy stays null
No work due at all: withheldByReason stays {} — the zero-count guard in withhold() already refuses a map of zeroes
An account that lapses mid-drip: its remaining rendered rows stay rendered, and the next tick after payment includes it in the scan again
One lapsed account holding 50 approvals no longer starves a healthy sibling account with an older approval

rollback_plan: No migration and no data change: the branch edits one read-only SELECT, one shared predicate's internals, and two CI audits. Revert the squash commit on main and redeploy the worker; the scan returns to its current shape on the next tick. No flag flip is needed, and SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED already gates P4 in production.
observability: withheldByReason.subscription on the Release cycle line is the new signal: a tick that releases nothing because every candidate account lapsed now names that gate instead of reading like an idle tick
withheldByReason.account_cap keeps its existing meaning, so the staging ramp's 'paced vs capped' read is unchanged
Silent-failure signal: a tick that logs released: 0 with withheldByReason {} and releasePhaseStoppedBy null while approved batches exist means an arm over-excluded or a counter went silent
